verdict.rationale: Kong documents running AI Gateway outside a SaaS context: there is a dedicated on-prem configuration page using AI plugins on Services and Routes, a self-run data plane in Docker with local log paths, and a hybrid architecture where the data plane carries the traffic. However, the evidence never clearly states that the full product, including the newer 2.x control plane and entity model, can be self-hosted rather than relying on Konnect. missing for 10: explicit self-hosted control-plane support for AI Gateway 2.x, production install/deployment guide, licensing/open-source terms for self-hosting, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: This page shows you how to configure the same capabilities with AI plugins on Services and Routes.
If you're running an AI Gateway data plane in Docker, you can also view them from your Docker container.
As in Kong Gateway hybrid mode, the control plane stays out of the data path
You can use the quickstart script to get a demo instance of AI Gateway running almost instantly.
